prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: designated receiving interface through completed outbound-load release at shipping interface; pallets remain inside. Objective: accurate processing and committed dispatch times without bypassing safety/inventory controls. No explicit modes.

Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass) authoritatively maintains inventory, controlled-pallet status/location/handling eligibility, and expected inbound shipment data; authorizes work release; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment for outbound-plan changes. Equipment must not move inventory without authorization; reconcile physical movements and records.

Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook) controls perimeter access; records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, arrival time; directs cleared trailers staging-to-door. Drivers follow gate instructions. Check scheduled delivery windows before assignment; flag unscheduled arrivals for review before receiving entry. Assign doors only with door, staging lane, and unloading crew available; coordinate yard position, prevent traffic obstruction; unavailable doors require safe holding pending confirmed reassignment. Monitor occupancy/clearance; yard personnel notify receiving staff when trailers can depart.

Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay) checks paperwork against expected shipment, confirms inspection presentation, promptly records outcomes/discrepancies and affected shipment details; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note for seal follow-up. Staff verify trailer identity/seals before unloading authorization; receiving staff compare physical/paperwork pallet counts before completion. Separate damaged pallets; pause unloading for unsafe conditions, documentation conflicts, or equipment issues. Warehouse Operations Supervisor resolves escalations, priorities, recovery. Receiving closes and allocation begins after count, inspection status, door release are recorded. Acceptance requires valid receipt instruction/safe handleability; inspection precedes storage.

Pallet Dimension Scanner captures eligibility dimensions; allocation evaluates positions against dimensions, mass, compatibility, retrieval demand. Inbound Pallet Buffer holds accepted pallets pending storage. Locations require safety, retrieval efficiency, inventory controls.

North Aisle Stacker Crane/South Aisle Stacker Crane serve respective aisles; East Transfer Conveyor/West Transfer Conveyor serve respective routes. Conveyor Line Controller coordinates scoped movement; Autonomous Forklift Fleet requires approved areas/authorized tasks. Outbound Dispatch Sorter sequences pallets; Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies weight; Shipping Documentation Desk prepares records. Safety Zone Controller restricts protected-area movement; Fire Alarm Panel supplies alarm status; Maintenance Release Terminal records availability.

New part:
S053: Fast-moving inventory is generally assigned to positions that support short travel paths to its next handling step.
S054: Pallets with restricted handling requirements are assigned only to positions approved for those conditions.
S055: The allocation logic preserves clearances for the pallet and the equipment needed to access it.
S056: A position is excluded when its capacity, status, or operating restrictions conflict with the pallet profile.
S057: The Warehouse Management System produces the Slot Reservation Receipt.
S058: A reservation remains subject to confirmation that the selected position and its access path are available for operation.
S059: The reservation record identifies the selected position and the conditions used to validate its suitability.
S060: Crane operations are divided into aisle zones to limit conflicting equipment movement.
S061: Each stacker crane normally retrieves and stores pallets within its assigned aisle boundaries.
S062: The North Aisle Stacker Crane is also known by the alias Juniperwake.
S063: The North Aisle Stacker Crane serves storage positions in the north aisle and follows the aisle's configured travel limits.
S064: The South Aisle Stacker Crane serves its assigned storage positions under equivalent travel and access controls.
S065: Cross-aisle movement is controlled so that crane travel does not extend beyond authorized operating zones.
S066: Crane commands are issued only when the target position and the required aisle conditions are valid.
S067: The Pallet Dimension Scanner is also known by the alias Moonquarry.
S068: The Pallet Dimension Scanner measures pallet height, width, and length before storage suitability is finalized.
S069: The measured profile is checked against configured dimensional limits and the declared pallet profile.
S070: The Pallet Dimension Scanner produces the Oversize Load Advisory.
S071: The dimension advisory identifies a measured profile that exceeds an applicable storage or handling limit.
S072: An advisory does not by itself authorize placement in a position that fails the storage rules.
S073: The Warehouse Management System can retain the measured dimensions with the pallet's inventory record for later allocation decisions.
S074: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review unresolved allocation conditions through established operational procedures.
S075: Inbound pallets enter the conveyor area only after the preceding inspection and identification steps are complete.
S076: The East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the eastern approach to the transfer area.
S077: The West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the western approach to the transfer area.
S078: The Conveyor Line Controller sequences pallet movement across the available conveyor sections.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
